VI. 1. 89</ls>; so दुःखः˚ काम˚. .{@-तम्@} {%ind.%} Rightly, properly. .{@-तः@} .²1 A sacrifice. .²2 The sun ({%n.%} also). .{@-तम्@} (Not usually found in classical literature) .²1 A fixed or settled rule, law (religious). .²2 Sacred custom, pious action. यस्तनोति सतां सेतुमृतेनामृतयोनिना <ls>Mb. 12. 47. 49</ls>. .²3 Divine law, divine truth. .²4 Absolution. मर्त्यानामृतमिच्छताम् <ls>Bhāg. 1. 16. 7</ls>. .²5 Water; सत्यं त्वा ऋतेन परिषिञ्चामि. .²6 Truth (in general), right; ऋतं वदिष्यामि <ls>T. Up. 1. 1. 1</ls>. ऋतानृते <ls>Ms. 1. 29</ls>, <ls n="Ms.">2. 52</ls>, <ls n="Ms.">8. 61</ls>, <ls n="Ms. 8.">104</ls>. .²7 Truth (personified as an object of worship; in later Sanskrit regarded as a child of Dharma). .²8 Livelihood by picking or gleaning grains in a field (as opposed to the cultivation of ground); ऋतमुञ्च्छशिलं वृत्तम् <ls>Ms. 4. 4</ls>. .²9 The fruit of an action; एकं चक्रं वर्तते द्वादशारं षण्णाभिमेकाक्षमृतस्य धारणम् <ls>Mb. 1. 3. 62</ls>. .²10 Agreeable speech; ऋतं च सूनृता वाणी कविभिः परिकीर्तिता <ls>Bhāg. 11. 19. 38</ls>. .²11 <ab>N.</ab> of an Āditya. .²12 The Supreme Spirit. (In the Vedas ऋत is usually interpreted by Sāyaṇa to mean ‘water’, ‘sun’ or ‘sacrifice’, where European scholars take it in the sense of ‘divine truth’, ‘faith’ <ab>&c.</ab>).
